I construct a zero-investment trading strategy based on buying an equally weighted portfolio of firms with low bankruptcy risk and shorting an equally weighted portfolio of firms with high bankruptcy risk.
Firms with low probability of bankruptcy are defined as the 70 percent of all firms with the lowest probability of bankruptcy.
Firms with high bankruptcy risk are defined monthly as firms in the top decile of bankruptcy risk in the full sample
buying an equally weighted portfolio of firms with low bankruptcy risk and shorting an equally weighted portfolio of firms with high bankruptcy risk.
Net Ret is the mean return on the low bankruptcy risk portfolio minus the mean return on the high bankruptcy risk portfolio.
the top and bottom 1 percent of observations for each variable, except market value, are set at the 1st and the 99th percentile respectively.
